chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

There is no person but that with him are two angels who write whatever he utters, then they send that up to two [other] angels above them who record what was good or evil from it, and cast aside anything other than that.
ai.seo_question: What do the angels record about a person's speech according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the hierarchical mechanism of divine recording, where initial utterances are captured by attendant angels and then filtered by superior angels to preserve only significant good and evil deeds. It highlights the Shia understanding of the 'Kiraman Katibin' not merely as passive recorders but as active evaluators who distinguish between trivial speech and weighty actions. This process underscores the precision of divine accounting, ensuring that only meaningful contributions to one's spiritual ledger are retained for the Day of Judgment.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 1.Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, “Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated to us from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Zurārah who said, “I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (a) say, ‘

There is no person but that with him are two angels who write whatever he utters, then they send that up to two [other] angels above them who record what was good or evil from it, and cast aside anything other than that.’”
